invariants.text: One row per log emitted by a seeded settlement contract. (block_timestamp, log_index) is both unique_key and the ReplacingMergeTree order_by, so count() - uniqExact((block_timestamp, log_index)) must be 0.

event_name IS NULL means a seeded settlement contract has no ABI in contracts_abi for chain='celo' — the address is scanned but matches no signature. Adding an address to celo_gpay_settlement_contracts REQUIRES fetching its ABI in the same change (fetch_abi_to_csv.py --chain celo --regen). Held at zero on 2026-08-06 — every topic0 either contract has ever emitted resolves to a declared ABI event. The candidate bridge 0xd11e35ca has emitted no logs at all, so it costs nothing to carry.

TokenPullSuccess is the authoritative charge. Count both sides up to least(max(activity.block_time), max(TokenPullSuccess.block_timestamp)) — either model can lag the other, so an activity-only watermark false-fails when settlement decode is behind (8-row surplus on 2026-08-07 when pull_wm trailed act_wm by ~35 min) and a pull-only watermark false-fails the other way. Unbounded comparison always shows a spurious surplus (172 on 2026-08-05). Enforced by celo_gpay_charges_match_payments.

The contracts share zero topic0s, but not because they are unrelated. Every event on settlement_current takes an extra indexed `sender` as its first parameter, which changes the canonical signature and so the hash. Function selectors are identical on both. Treat them as two generations of one design that need two ABIs, not as two different systems.

Everything pulled from cards is settled out — the contract holds no float. Summing TokenPullSuccess.amount against SettlementBridged plus SettlementTransferred gives a residual of 0.00 on BOTH contracts (settlement_current 257,965.79 in against 172,558.87 bridged + 85,406.92 local; settlement_legacy 75,962.09 against 58,034.40 + 17,927.70), re-verified 2026-08-06. CHECK IT AT CONTRACT LEVEL, NOT PER TOKEN. Per token it fails on settlement_legacy, and that failure is a decode fault rather than a retained balance — see legacy-mislabels-the-pulled-token. All amounts are 6-decimal here because only USDC and USDT settle; a token with different decimals would need per-token scaling before this check means anything.

settlement_legacy reports the WRONG token on TokenPullSuccess. All 1,752 of its pulls decode as USDC, while raw ERC-20 Transfer logs show 345 USDC and 1,407 USDT actually arriving — and 17,927,696,109 + 58,034,396,265 is exactly the 75,962,092,374 the events attribute to USDC alone. Counts and amounts are correct, only the token field lies, and it lies consistently rather than randomly, so nothing looks corrupt. settlement_current is unaffected (1,087 USDC and 2,505 USDT, and per-token conservation holds there exactly, which is the tell). Outbound events carry the right token on BOTH contracts, verified the same way. So never derive a per-token charge breakdown from this model — take the amount from the event and the token from the transfer. Discovered 2026-08-06 by ground-truthing against transfers; docs/lessons/event-field-can-lie.md. NOT a decode fault on our side, which was checked explicitly because indexed flags do not enter topic0 and a wrong flag would read the wrong bytes while still appearing to decode. Our ABI marks rolesModifier and token indexed with amount in data, and the raw logs carry exactly topic1, topic2 and one 64-char data word. topic2 is the token slot and it holds USDC in all 1,758 legacy events and USDT in none, so the constant is written by the contract. Re-verified against a public Celo node with no warehouse involvement — tx 0x7b84681b… at block 73731678 has the event naming USDC for 13,070,000 while the only inbound transfer is USD₮ for exactly 13,070,000. Two controls decode correctly through the same code path (legacy 0x22cc85f1… where the token really is USDC, and current-contract 0x5c86713f… carrying USD₮), which is what rules out a decoder fault rather than a contract one. Exhaustively scanned 2026-08-07 by matching every pull to the transfer of the same amount in the same transaction, both contracts, full history. It is NOT intermittent — the legacy token field is effectively a constant. Across all 1,769 of its pulls the field has only ever held USDC and has never once held USDT, so it is wrong on 1,422 of 1,769 (80.4%) and right on the other 347 only because the real token happened to be USDC. The rate tracks the USDT share of spend, not any change in the contract, and is present from its first month (2026-03, 2 of 4 wrong) to its most recent charges. settlement_current is wrong on 0 of 3,764 and emits both tokens (1,122 USDC, 2,642 USDT). Every pull on both contracts matched a real transfer, so there is no unexplained residue.

Batches run roughly 7 times a day (mean 6.4 over the trailing 30 days, range 4 to 9), NOT twice as recorded here until 2026-08-06 — the earlier reading came from the 01:00 and 13:00 peaks and missed the rest. Cadence has risen with volume, and batch size with it (median 7 charges, p90 36, max 76). This is why an unbounded comparison against any point-in-time model shows a surplus, and why a Celo GP figure built mid-afternoon differs from the same figure built at midnight.

Every one of the 476 settlement transactions contains BOTH the TokenPullSuccess charges and the settlement outflow; there is no transaction that does only one. Cards are charged and the money leaves in the same transaction, so charge-to-settlement lag is zero by construction and value in flight never exists. Do not build a lag or float mart on this model — that was scoped and abandoned 2026-08-06 for exactly this reason. The only residual is cross-token, where about 10 percent of (transaction, token) charge groups pull a token that transaction does not settle and it waits for the next sweep.

TokenPullFailedWithAmount has fired 7 times (5 legacy, 2 current); the richer TokenPullFailed with its errorData payload never has. On legacy every instance had remainingAmount equal to originAmount, meaning nothing was pulled at all; the two on 2026-06-29 were partial, pulling some and leaving a remainder. These are charge attempts that moved no money, so nothing in the transfer-derived tree can see them — do not treat them as payments, and do not expect them to reconcile against anything in int_celo_gpay_activity.

TokenPullSuccess.rolesModifier is the card's Zodiac Roles module and normally resolves in int_celo_gpay_roles_modules, but this model follows head while that one is built at a point in time, so charges by cards provisioned since its last build do not resolve yet. 8 of 5,338 on 2026-08-06, every one of them from the 01:00 batch that ran after the registry's 2026-08-05 09:44 watermark. Bound any completeness check at that watermark, exactly as the mastercopy drift probe does, or read ordinary issuance as breakage.

invariants.text: One row per emitted log. (block_timestamp, transaction_hash, log_index) is both the unique_key and the ReplacingMergeTree order_by, so count() - uniqExact((block_timestamp, transaction_hash, log_index)) must be 0.

event_name must never be empty. An empty event_name means the ABI join missed, which happens silently with no error - the usual cause is contracts_hopr_registry.abi_source_address pointing at an implementation address instead of the proxy. The `no undecoded rows` query in validation below is the check.

THREE HOPR environments live on Gnosis Chain simultaneously (dufour, jura and the rotsee testnet) and dufour emits the same logical events under DIFFERENT topic0s than the v4 pair. The ABI resolves per contract address, so a single-ABI decode would silently drop an environment entirely. Each v4 environment was also REDEPLOYED once, so a network has more than one contract_address. Assert uniqExact(network) == 3 and check presence per network -- never a bare address count.

jura's Announcements is an EIP-1967 proxy (implementation 0x914c4ad36e5ec147be0a94c671d7440f1d0fc8c1) but its event_signatures rows are keyed on the PROXY address, because fetch_abi_to_csv.py stores the implementation's ABI under the proxy's contract_address. Setting abi_source_address to the implementation makes the ABI join miss and produced 59 rows with empty event_name and no error.

contract.reprocess_runbook: Rebuild with scripts/full_refresh/refresh.py (a plain `dbt run --full- refresh` also works but re-scans the whole logs history in one query). Because the strategy is append, drop target partitions first (macros/db/drop_partition.sql) if they already hold rows. Changing contracts_hopr_registry_static or the oracle ABI names requires `dbt seed` FIRST - refresh.py rebuilds models only, and a stale registry yields silently undecoded rows.

hazards.title: An incremental model created before its input existed stays empty forever
Code 241 with a "(total)" server-wide limit means your query is the victim, not the culprit
Staged/batched refreshes against insert_overwrite models wipe months via REPLACE PARTITION
>100 partitions per INSERT fails (252) and Cloud blocks raising the cap (452)
Scoped append over already-populated months exactly doubles the data
Backfill order matters — cumulative downstreams need history first
Stage start_date later than real first activity silently truncates history
Duplicate seed rows in an append chain carry a constant error forward every day
A cumulative chain that builds the frontier day before its inputs settle freezes the hole

After first build, verify the table is non-empty: a green daily run on an empty incremental stays empty forever (bootstrap can't reach history).
The strategy branches on run vars: scoped windows must take the append path and append only into EMPTY months; verify which branch a given invocation resolves to before running.
Cumulative: backfill history FIRST, chronologically. Forward runs never repair a wrong initial condition; a duplicate seed row propagates forever.

A frontier day built before its inputs settled stays frozen forever (the incremental branch never revisits it) even after the upstream self-heals — repair with the model's reprocess window, not the daily runner.

hazards.title: An incremental model created before its input existed stays empty forever
Code 241 with a "(total)" server-wide limit means your query is the victim, not the culprit
Staged/batched refreshes against insert_overwrite models wipe months via REPLACE PARTITION
Scoped append over already-populated months exactly doubles the data
Backfill order matters — cumulative downstreams need history first
Stage start_date later than real first activity silently truncates history
Duplicate seed rows in an append chain carry a constant error forward every day
A cumulative chain that builds the frontier day before its inputs settle freezes the hole

rules.text: Never a wide delete+insert — the background delete can complete after dbt reports failure and silently wipe the window; reprocess per slice/partition.
insert_overwrite REPLACEs whole partitions: partition grain must equal the overwrite grain; never combine with unique_key, slice vars, or staged batches.
Follow the required workflow in AGENTS.md; check docs/lessons/INDEX.md before diagnosing a data-quality symptom.
After first build, verify the table is non-empty: a green daily run on an empty incremental stays empty forever (bootstrap can't reach history).
The strategy branches on run vars: scoped windows must take the append path and append only into EMPTY months; verify which branch a given invocation resolves to before running.
Cumulative: backfill history FIRST, chronologically. Forward runs never repair a wrong initial condition; a duplicate seed row propagates forever.

A frontier day built before its inputs settled stays frozen forever (the incremental branch never revisits it) even after the upstream self-heals — repair with the model's reprocess window, not the daily runner.

invariants.text: Grain is (network, date); count() must equal uniqExact((network, date)). The date spine is a UNION DISTINCT of the three inputs' own dates, so a duplicate means an input started emitting more than one row per day.

nodes_registered_cumulative counts nodes that ever key-bound and never decrements. nodes_online_avg counts nodes up on the day. Presenting the first as network size overstates HOPR several-fold, and the factor grows every year. Any single "node count" on a dashboard must name which one.

The registrations CTE joins decoded events to contracts_hopr_registry. execution.logs carries addresses as BARE hex while the registry stores them 0x-prefixed, so the join must strip the prefix (lower(contract_address) = replaceAll(r.address, '0x', '')). Joining raw matches nothing, yields a cumulative count of zero for every date, and still builds green -- this exact failure happened during development.

The dashboard's hourly history is missing a substantial share of its hours, so a day can rest on anything from one observation to twenty-four. Read nodes_online_avg together with hours_observed and drop or flag thin days; averaging them as equal to full days silently overweights sparse periods.
NULL in any prober column means no measurement existed for that day, never zero nodes. coalescing them to 0 would invent an outage across the whole span before the ingestor started.

contract.reprocess_runbook: Plain `dbt run --select fct_hopr_network_health_daily` - it is a small table rebuilt whole with no watermark. Rebuild after the click-runner HOPR ingestors run or after any Announcements decode change. Set DBT_HOPR_SCHEMA to the database holding the click-runner tables when building outside prod.

invariants.text: One row per classified transfer. The upstream base carries both Safe sides of a Safe-to-Safe transfer; this model keeps the sender ('out') side so each transfer is a single row (a Withdrawal). The grain omits log_index, so two transfers of the same token to the same counterparty in one tx collapse under ReplacingMergeTree — acceptable only while no such pattern exists on Celo GP.

Restricted to whitelisted tokens via token_symbol IS NOT NULL, which drops CELO gas dust and spoof tokens. Anything unpriced or unknown-decimals belongs upstream in int_celo_gpay_safe_transfers_alltoken, never here. Payment is card -> settlement contract in a STABLECOIN. The same flow in a non-stablecoin whitelisted token is 'Other' and must stay out of payment metrics. Cashback is compiled out until the model's cashback_sources list is populated, so reward inflows currently classify as Top-up.

invariants.text: The card population is the union over every settlement contract in celo_gpay_settlement_contracts with status active or migrating. Never hardcode a bridge address in this tree and never narrow the set to one — doing exactly that omitted 235 cards and a third of all settlement traffic until 2026-08-05, and made a product that had run since March look like it launched in June. Adding GP's migration target must be a seed edit only. See docs/lessons/circular-completeness-proof.md.

This registry decides which Safes exist; int_celo_gpay_activity decides what their transfers mean. Both read the same seed and must change in the same run. Widening discovery alone admits cards whose settlement transfers then fall through to the catch-all and book as Withdrawals, which inflates withdrawals while still under-reporting payments — strictly worse than omitting those cards.

GP will migrate the legacy cards onto the current contract, so a card can settle to different bridges over its life. Membership therefore belongs on the transfer (int_celo_gpay_activity.settlement_address), never as a per-card generation column, which would go stale the day that card moves. Migration state is readable from int_celo_gpay_roles_modules.wired_settlements — a module listing two addresses has migrated; zero had on 2026-08-05.

invariants.text: One row per (date, validator_index) for EVERY validator in that day's int_consensus_validators_snapshots_daily, including exited and zero-balance (~558k/day). A day holding fewer rows means one or more validator_index band slices silently inserted nothing; downstream per_index/dists marts then aggregate a biased cohort (2026-07 served a NEGATIVE network APY off one mostly-exited band).

balance_prev_gno and every cumulative_* column chain from the previous day via lagInFrame + prev_state from the target table. Never build a day before its predecessor exists for that band — a missing prior day makes balance_prev fall back to 0, the effective-credit formula absorbs the whole balance, and income pins at the spec cap (~35.7 APY for 56k validators on 2026-07-20) while cumulatives reset to zero.

Every apply_monthly_incremental_filter call in this model MUST pass filters_sql=range_sql — including CTEs whose source has no validator_index (network_state). The range scope applies to the target-table watermark subquery; without it the CTE watermarks off the global frontier and later-band slices compile to an empty window, inserting 0 rows while dbt reports success.

consensus_income_amount_gno <= expected_reward_cap_gno except for real slashing losses; never re-derive income from balance deltas plus reported deposits alone (post-Pectra queue-drain days break it).

contract.reprocess_runbook: Damage is month-partition-contained. rules.text: Never a wide delete+insert — the background delete can complete after dbt reports failure and silently wipe the window; reprocess per slice/partition.
insert_overwrite REPLACEs whole partitions: partition grain must equal the overwrite grain; never combine with unique_key, slice vars, or staged batches.
Follow the required workflow in AGENTS.md; check docs/lessons/INDEX.md before diagnosing a data-quality symptom.
Cumulative: backfill history FIRST, chronologically. Forward runs never repair a wrong initial condition; a duplicate seed row propagates forever.

A frontier day built before its inputs settled stays frozen forever (the incremental branch never revisits it) even after the upstream self-heals — repair with the model's reprocess window, not the daily runner.

invariants.text: Each run emits ONLY today's rows, and Discourse exposes views/reads as current totals with no per-event endpoint. A day this model did not run is permanently absent and cannot be reconstructed from any source. Do not interpolate across a gap and do not treat the series as continuous without checking snapshot_date coverage first.

Unlike every other incremental model in this project, `dbt run --full-refresh` on this one DESTROYS data: it drops the accumulated daily history and re-emits a single day (today). There is no recovery. Rebuild requests for this model must be refused.

partition_by is snapshot_date, deliberately NOT toStartOfMonth. Because insert_overwrite REPLACEs whole partitions present in the batch and each run emits only today's rows, a month-grain partition would wipe every earlier day of the current month on every run. Daily partitions make a re-run overwrite exactly its own day, which is what makes it idempotent. The cost is one partition per day (ch-partition-cap), accepted knowingly.

snapshot_date is the day we LOOKED; observed_at is when the value was actually true. Ingestion re-reads a topic only when bumped_at beats the watermark, so a dormant thread's counter is frozen at its last activity. A difference between two consecutive snapshot_dates is real change ONLY if observed_at also moved; otherwise the grid is repeating a stale number.

Scope is the two counters that cannot be recovered retroactively. Likes are deliberately excluded because they have a per-event endpoint (/user_actions.json), so their full history with timestamps and actors is backfillable into stg_governance__forum_likes. Adding a like counter here would be strictly worse information at higher cost.

contract.reprocess_runbook: There is nothing to backfill and nothing to full-refresh — see the full-refresh-is-destructive-here invariant. Re-running today is safe and idempotent: insert_overwrite replaces only today's snapshot_date partition. If a past day is missing, it stays missing; record the gap rather than filling it. Never change partition_by to a month grain. Nothing reads this model yet, so a re-run has no downstream rebuild.

contract.ground_truth: On-chain HoprAnnouncements / HoprNodeSafeRegistry / HoprNodeStakeFactory events, plus the hopr_node_registry seed for class labels and crawlers_data.ipinfo for geography.

hazards.title: LEFT JOIN misses return defaults, not NULLs — set join_use_nulls in a pre_hook
Append decode watermark drops late-arriving logs forever
argMax "latest/quarter-end" marts silently serve the last ingested day when a source halts

invariants.text: Grain is (network, node_address); count() must equal uniqExact((network, node_address)). A duplicate would double-count a node in every operator-concentration or geography aggregate.

join_use_nulls = 1 must stay set in the pre_hook. Every enrichment is a LEFT JOIN and ClickHouse otherwise fills unmatched rows with the column TYPE DEFAULT ('' for String), not NULL. Without it every unclassified node reads as classified, and every node reports geo enrichment whether or not ipinfo matched. Both failures are silent.

ipinfo coverage of HOPR IPs depends on ip_crawler having been pointed at them IN THE DATABASE BEING READ, and the two databases differ. crawlers_data is populated by the nebula pipeline for a different node set, so it contains HOPR IPs only incidentally; playground_max is where ip_crawler's `hopr` preset has been run. Until that preset runs against crawlers_data, expect geo_source to be mostly 'unenriched' on a prod build and mostly 'ipinfo' in dev -- that gap is missing ingestion, not a regression in this model. Coverage also lags newly-announced IPs between crawler runs. Never filter unenriched nodes out of counts, and never read a NULL ip_country as "no country".

count() here is "nodes that EVER registered", never "network size" -- on-chain presence is cumulative and never expires, so nodes that stopped running years ago still count. It runs several times the live network.
Judging which rows are alive takes two signals, not one. liveness_source = 'prober' with is_reachable is direct evidence of life, but the prober's roster is not the population of record: some unprobed nodes still earn on chain, so last_channel_activity_at is the second signal and neither alone is sufficient. fct_hopr_network_health_daily holds registered and online side by side.

This model reads stg_hopr_db__network_nodes, so it depends on click-runner's HOPR tables existing in whatever database the source resolves to (hopr_db by default, DBT_HOPR_SCHEMA to override). A ClickHouse view over a missing table fails to CREATE rather than returning nothing, so if those tables are absent the build errors instead of degrading. The whole HOPR set is still development-only, so nothing is live yet -- but the first production build will fail unless the tables exist in hopr_db. A single run of each click-runner HOPR ingestor creates them (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS); the cron does not have to be deployed first. Same applies to fct_hopr_network_health_daily, the api_hopr_* views and the four stg_hopr_db__* views.

NodeSafeRegistry is the ONLY source linking a node to a Safe. NewHoprNodeStakeSafe carries just `instance` (the Safe address) and no node address, so it can only date a Safe's creation, never attribute it.

dufour emits DergisteredNodeSafe (a typo in the deployed contract) and jura emits DeregisteredNodeSafe. Matching one spelling silently under-counts deregistrations on the other network, inflating is_registered.
